limitations: This lifecycle applies only to the recorded Native Bridge v12 evidence and must not be normalized into NTT digest semantics.
A successful inbound system receipt or sequence advance does not alone prove ERC-20 delivery.

directions.sourceEvidence: A successful Ethereum receipt with AssetsLocked(sequence, recipient, sourceToken, amount).
directions.messageEvidence: The source tuple is included in the validator-canonicalized sequence consumed by the Mezo pre-block handler.
directions.destinationEvidence: The matching Mezo system bridge payload and sequence advancement plus recipient balance/post-state delivery for the mapped representation.
directions.warning: System-receipt success or sequence advancement alone is insufficient for ERC-20 delivery because the deployed keeper may skip an unmapped/blocked/failed mint while continuing the sequence.

directions.sourceEvidence: A successful Mezo bridgeOut receipt with AssetsUnlocked(sequence, recipient, targetToken, sender, amount, chain).
directions.messageEvidence: Ethereum AssetsUnlockAttested for the same sequence and tuple.
directions.destinationEvidence: A successful Ethereum receipt with AssetsUnlockConfirmed for the same tuple plus recipient asset delivery; fee-adjusted net delivery must reconcile to the gross source amount.
directions.warning: An attestation is progress, not completion; reconcile the confirmation event and delivered asset.

reconciliationRequirements: Assert Ethereum and Mezo network identity independently and pin every observation to a block coordinate.
Join the provider sequence and full direction-specific tuple; do not apply an NTT digest join to Native Bridge.
Treat absent destination evidence as pending or ambiguous, not failed.
For inbound ERC-20 delivery, require recipient post-state or equivalent mint/delivery proof beyond the logless system transaction.
For outbound delivery, separate gross amount, withdrawal fee, and recipient net amount and require exact reconciliation.
Re-read active proxy implementation, mappings, minima, capacity, pause/validator state, fee, recipient encoding, and allowance/authorization requirements before future writes.
